messages:
PagerDuty: :rotating_light: URGENT: control-plane errors rising — 5xx rate ~38% over last 3m (auth/org-lookup backend). Pager trigger: multi-service spike. Escalation policy: oncall -> eng-sre.

Alex (oncall): taking this. Observed 502/504 primarily from /v1/auth/validate-token and /v1/org/lookup. Dashboards: https://dash.redwood.app/d/ctrlplane/errors (spike at 00:12 UTC).

Priya: seeing same. User-facing errors reported by convo-service + gateway timeouts. Could be auth fanout amplification — if auth times out, gateway returns 502.

Sam: pulling logs now. sample curl to auth endpoint returns 502 consistently:

```
$ curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer xxxxx" https://control.redwood.internal/v1/auth/validate-token
HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
Content-Type: application/json
{"error":"upstream error: org-lookup timed out"}
```

Sam: org-lookup backend latency shows p95 jump from 80ms -> 2.4s and many connection resets.

Jordan: any recent deploys to controlplane or org service in last 30m? OpsBot deploy-log: deploys: none in last 60m. Config-change?

OpsBot: recent config change: routing flag `org_lookup_parallelism` set to 6 -> 12 at 00:05 UTC by feature-ops. (link: https://git.redwood/app/ops/flags/123)

Alex (oncall): that could be it. If org lookup parallelism increased, backend may be overwhelmed causing timeouts and cascading 5xx. Priya, can we circuit-break or reduce fanout at gateway?

Priya: Yes. Two immediate mitigations: 1) flip `org_lookup_parallelism` back to 6, 2) enable short-lived cache for org results (fallback TTL 30s) at gateway to reduce calls. I can push both as a fast config rollback.

Sam: while you flip, I'll add temporary retry/backoff on auth calls to avoid hammering org. Also raising connection pool limits on org micro to 300 from 100 as quick protective measure.

Alex (oncall): Good. Also patch gateway to return 503 with Retry-After instead of 502 for degraded state so clients can back off.

Maya: Notifying CS and engineering leads. ETA to rollback and cache change?

Priya: Rolling rollback now (will run canary then full). Command: `kubectl set env deploy/ctrl-gateway ORG_LOOKUP_PARALLELISM=6 --namespace=controlplane` then configmap bump for cache.

Sam: Adding these logs while change goes out:
```
[00:14:02] rollback job started
[00:14:38] canary passed (3/3 checks)
[00:15:12] full rollout initiated
[00:15:45] cache config applied: ORG_CACHE_TTL=30s
```

Priya: Done. Flag reverted and cache enabled. Monitoring now.

Alex (oncall): Traffic trending back down. 5xx rate dropped to 6% in last 2m. p95 org lookup at ~110ms now. Good sign.

Jordan: Can we set circuit-breaker at gateway so a single auth/org backend doesn't fan out to many downstream services? Propose: max_concurrent=8, fail-open to cached response.

Priya: Agree. I'll schedule followup change for durable circuit-breaker and add automations to detect parallelism spikes.

Maya: CS: notifying affected customers with note: transient auth/lookup errors between 00:05-00:16 UTC, most requests retried successfully. Asking for any customer cases to escalate.

Customer Success Bot: created support ticket #CS-4721 for customers reporting 502s.

Alex (oncall): Post-incident actions (short list):
- Create a guardrail for parallelism flag (max=8)
- Add synthetic heartbeat for org-lookup to detect slowdowns earlier
- Add automated rollback when p50 > 200ms or 5xx rate > 10% for 2m after flag change
- Postmortem owner: Priya

Sam: capturing error samples and correlation IDs for postmortem. Will attach traces.

Priya: assigning postmortem — will draft and share in #postmortems. Severity set to P2 due to partial customer impact but no prolonged outage.

Alex (oncall): Thanks all. Leaving note: oncall monitoring for next 2 hours. If 5xx crosses 10% again, re-escalate to SRE lead. :thumbsup:

OpsBot: Incident closed in channel at 00:18 UTC (auto-comment). Follow-up tasks created: OPS-881, CS-4721, PM-299.

Maya: Great coordination — thanks. Priya please ping when postmortem is ready.

Priya: Will do, aiming for draft within 24h.

Alex (oncall): closing thread. :pray:
